subject: SLO measurement: sampling & truncation rules for p50/p95
messages:

To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify how p95 is counted during our payroll spike

Hi Marissa,

Quick question as we finalize the SLO section in the order form: during our monthly payroll run we see a very short but sharp traffic spike (~20 minutes) where 10-15% of requests show much higher latency. Does Redwood compute p95 over raw request samples (including those short spikes), or do you aggregate into time buckets and then roll those buckets into the 30-day window?

Specifically:
- Will that 20-minute spike be reflected in the 30-day p95 and potentially trigger credits?
- Do streaming responses get truncated for latency measurement (we have a lot of long streaming completions)?

We're trying to map expected credits to expected worst-case runs. Attached is a small traffic snapshot from last month's run.

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Dawson
Head of Platform Reliability, FinBank

Subject: Re: Clarify how p95 is counted during our payroll spike

Jane — thanks for the snapshot, very helpful. looping in Karthik and Ben to confirm our exact measurement rules and whether we can do a narrow carveout for your predictable payroll window.

Quick answers while they chime in:
- We compute p50/p95 from production request latencies but we use an aggregation pipeline (per-minute histograms) before rolling into the 30-day reporting window. That generally dampens single-minute noise, but sustained 20-minute spikes can still influence the reported percentiles.
- Streaming completions are measured end-to-end by default; there is an option to report "initial response" latencies instead, which some customers prefer for UX-facing SLOs.

Kar/Ben — can you confirm the exact sampling rate, how we treat cold starts and model-rotation warm-ups, and whether we can offer a time-boxed carveout for FinBank's payroll event?

—Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jane Dawson <jane.dawson@finbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify how p95 is counted during our payroll spike

Hi all — thanks for the clear ask and the sample, Jane. I'll lay out the current measurement rules and a pragmatic carveout proposal.

Measurement summary (current default):
- Sampling & aggregation: we ingest raw request latencies at 100% and aggregate them into per-minute histograms on the edge (these are not downsampled). From there we compute per-minute percentiles (p50/p95).
- Rolling window: the SLO reported value is the percentile computed over the union of per-minute aggregates across a rolling 30-day window. Practically that means a short sustained burst (e.g., 20 minutes) can move the 30-day p95, though single isolated minutes are less impactful because they become a small fraction of the window.
- Streaming/truncation: for streaming completions we support two measurement modes: (A) end-to-end completion latency (default), and (B) initial-token latency (time to first completed token). Mode selection is a customer-level flag; default is (A) unless you opt-in to (B).
- Cold starts and model swaps: we detect model worker restarts and exclude the first 5 minutes after a hot-standby rotation from SLO computation (warm-up carveout). This is automated.
- Synthetic/internal probes: traffic identified with UA or API key tagged as 'probe' is filtered out before aggregation.

Proposal for FinBank payroll run:
- We can offer a time-boxed carveout for recurring, scheduled payroll windows up to 4 hours per month where we will exclude those per-minute aggregates from the p95 calculation, provided: (a) the window is scheduled in advance and (b) traffic shape matches the attached snapshot.
- If the payroll run exceeds 4 hours or deviates materially, we'll treat the excess as normal traffic.
- For streaming-heavy requests during that window you can elect to switch to initial-token latency reporting for the payroll job (reduces measured tail).
- To operationalize: we will accept a calendar-based entitle (timezone-aware) and require 48h notice for any change. We'll also request a one-time sample run for us to validate.

If you need credits tied to that carveout, we should scope that in the contract (Ben can propose language/credits). Otherwise this is an operational SLO exclusion.

—Karthik
Sr. Product Manager, Inference Metrics

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Dawson <jane.dawson@finbank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-10T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify how p95 is counted during our payroll spike

Jane — from legal/ops side, the carveout Karthik describes is a standard operational exclusion we can attach as an appendix. A few practical notes:
- We'll document the calendar windows in the order form and add the 48h-change control.
- Credit vs carveout: we typically offer either (1) a carveout (no credits) or (2) a credit schedule if you want the window counted but compensated. For scheduled payroll spikes we recommend the carveout unless you want SLA credit economics — that increases contract complexity.
- I'll attach a short draft (proposed_carveout_terms.pdf) with credit tiers if you'd rather go that route.

If that works I'll prepare the appendix and route for signature.

Thanks,
Ben
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_carveout_terms.pdf (pdf, 62KB)

From: Jane Dawson <jane.dawson@finbank.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify how p95 is counted during our payroll spike

Marissa / Karthik / Ben — this is helpful, thank you. We prefer the operational carveout (simpler). A couple of follow-ups before we sign:
- Can you confirm the exact aggregation interval you use for per-minute histograms (is it 60s wall-clock or sliding windows?) and how you handle requests split across multiple connections (streaming chunks)?
- We'll provide recurring calendar windows for the next 12 months and the 48h notice is acceptable.
- We'll take the validation run next Thursday (2027-05-20). Can you confirm somebody from Redwood SRE will be on the call?

Looking forward to the appendix.

Best,
Jane
Head of Platform Reliability, FinBank
